questions.q: What is a hypervisor, in the context of building a home security lab?
options: Software like VirtualBox or VMware that runs one or more virtual machines on a single physical computer
A type of firewall rule used only inside Kali Linux
A vulnerability scanner built into Metasploitable2
A physical network switch required for lab isolation
questions.explain: A hypervisor is the software layer that lets one computer host several virtual machines at once, which is what a home lab is built on.

questions.q: Why is Metasploitable2 included in a basic home lab setup?
options: It's an intentionally vulnerable Linux VM, giving you a legal target to scan and exploit with Kali
It's a firewall that blocks all scanning attempts automatically
It replaces the need for a hypervisor entirely
It encrypts all lab traffic by default
questions.explain: Metasploitable2 is published by Rapid7 specifically to be exploited, giving learners a safe, legal, documented target.

questions.q: Why should lab VMs use a Host-Only or Internal Network adapter instead of Bridged?
options: Host-Only/Internal keeps traffic confined to the host machine, while Bridged exposes it to the real home network and internet
Bridged mode is required for Kali Linux to function at all
Host-Only mode is faster but has no effect on network isolation
There is no real difference between the two settings
questions.explain: Bridged mode puts a VM directly on the real network, which defeats the entire purpose of an isolated lab for live attack traffic.

questions.q: What does taking a snapshot of a VM let you do?
options: Instantly roll the VM back to a saved state after an experiment breaks something
Permanently delete the VM's virtual disk
Bridge the VM onto the real internet safely
Automatically patch the VM's vulnerabilities
questions.explain: A snapshot saves a VM's state so you can revert instantly instead of rebuilding a broken VM from scratch.

questions.q: What is the one rule that determines whether running these exact same tools and techniques is legal?
options: Whether you own the target system or have explicit written authorization to test it
Whether you're using Kali Linux instead of another operating system
Whether the attack happens during business hours
Whether the target system is running Windows or Linux
questions.explain: The techniques themselves are identical whether practiced legally or illegally — authorization over the target system is what makes the difference.
